effective_date_basis: The earliest of: own terms, revocation, completion, the end of the order's statutory authority under the 1921 resolution or the Knox-Porter / treaty dates (shown for that authority).
ending_pattern: Candidate end: the joint resolution of March 3, 1921 (Pub. Res. 64, 41 Stat. 1359-1360, event X1-E1) operates generally on any provision contingent on the duration or termination of the war or of the 'present or existing emergency', and on Acts in force only during the war; it names exceptions (among them the Trading with the Enemy Act, the District of Columbia rents title, the Liberty Bond Acts and parts of the War Finance Corporation Act). It ends the war-contingent statutory authority, not each order automatically. Other candidate dates: the Knox-Porter Resolution of July 2, 1921 (42 Stat. 105) and the peace treaties with Germany and Austria (proclaimed November 1921) and Hungary (proclaimed December 20, 1921), for statutes keyed to them; Acts with their own termination clauses (for example the Overman Act, six months after the war). Many orders ended earlier by revocation or completion.

exceptions_savings.assessment: Contracts, claims and property transfers made during the war are accrued effects; corporations or agencies created under wartime orders may have continued under later liquidation statutes (the exemplar's United States Housing Corporation was a New York corporation).

legal_effect: Research pattern only. A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order, and never substitutes for reading the order's own text.
outlier_conditions: The order's own text (not only the WPA summary or APP title) does not match the type, or the held text is another order's.
The order does more than the type's single act (a second operative clause of another kind).
A later order or statute amends, extends, revokes or revives it before the candidate end.
The order states its own effective date, duration, condition or termination that differs from the pattern.
Orders under the excepted statutes (the Trading with the Enemy Act among them).
Orders whose authority is not contingent on the war or the existing emergency: the 1921 resolution does not reach them.
Corporations or agencies created under wartime orders that continued under later liquidation statutes.
